An upper GI endoscopy reveals multiple deep ulcers in the second part of the duodenum and the distal esophagus. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the suspected underlying diagnosis?

A 45-year-old female presents with a persistent gritty sensation in her eyes, as if there is "sand" under her lids, and a dry mouth that requires her to sip water frequently while eating. On physical examination, she has bilateral, non-tender enlargement of the parotid glands. She also mentions occasional joint pain in her hands. Which of the following is the best next step in the clinical evaluation to objectively assess her primary complaint?

A 34-year-old male with a 10-year history of Ulcerative Colitis (currently in clinical remission on mesalamine) presents with progressive fatigue and intense generalized itching (pruritus) that is worse at night. Physical examination reveals excoriations on his arms and legs but no jaundice. Laboratory studies show a markedly elevated Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) and GGT, with only mildly elevated transaminases. An initial ultrasound shows no gallstones and no evidence of extrahepatic biliary duct obstruction. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-year-old tall, thin male presents to the Emergency Department with sudden-onset, sharp right-sided chest pain and severe shortness of breath that began acutely while he was climbing stairs. On examination, he is tachycardic, hypotensive, and has a deviated trachea. His chest X-ray reveals a mediastinal shift toward the left and a completely collapsed right lung. Given the clinical presentation and radiological findings, what is the most likely cause of his current acute distress?

A 16-year-old girl presents with chronic epigastric pain and a "pins and needles" sensation (paresthesia) in her hands and feet. Physical examination reveals a smooth, beefy red tongue (glossitis) and mild pallor. Laboratory investigations confirm a macrocytic anemia and significantly low serum Vitamin B12 levels. Given the combination of gastrointestinal symptoms and neurological deficits in a young patient, which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 26-year-old female presents with a persistent malar rash, photosensitivity, and swelling in the small joints of her hands. Laboratory testing is positive for ANA (1:640, speckled pattern) and anti-dsDNA antibodies, confirming a diagnosis of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). During a follow-up visit, the physician emphasizes the importance of monitoring for systemic organ involvement. Which of the following organ systems, if involved, is the major determinant of a poor long-term prognosis and increased mortality in this patient?

A 26-year-old female presents with a 3-week history of fever and productive cough, which has progressed to significant shortness of breath (SOB) over the last 4 days. On physical examination, there is decreased chest expansion on the affected side and a characteristic stony dull note on percussion. Which of the following is the best initial investigation to confirm the suspected diagnosis?

A 68-year-old male with long-standing hypertension is currently managed with Lisinopril (an ACE inhibitor) and Chlorthalidone (a thiazide-like diuretic). At a follow-up visit, his blood pressure is well-controlled at 120/85. However, he reports recent recurrent episodes of dizziness, confusion, and a persistent headache. He is brought to the Emergency Room after a syncopal episode; his heart rate is found to be 35 bpm (severe bradycardia). Which of the following electrolyte abnormalities is most likely responsible for this clinical presentation?

A 32-year-old male presents for a routine physical examination. The physician notes yellowish, slightly raised plaques on the medial aspect of his upper eyelids and a whitish-grey ring at the periphery of both corneas. The patient mentions that his father died of a myocardial infarction at age 42. Laboratory studies reveal a total cholesterol of 380 mg/dL and an LDL-cholesterol of 310 mg/dL, while triglycerides are within the normal range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old male who recently underwent a mechanical mitral valve replacement is started on long-term Warfarin therapy for stroke prophylaxis. Four weeks later, he presents to the clinic with scattered petechiae on his trunk and lower extremities. Laboratory studies reveal a significantly elevated Prothrombin Time (PT) and an International Normalized Ratio (INR) of 5.8 (therapeutic range is 2.5–3.5 for mechanical mitral valves). Which of the following is the underlying mechanism for his current presentation?

A 4-day-old infant is brought to the pediatric clinic for a routine newborn follow-up. On cardiovascular examination, a harsh, holosystolic murmur is heard loudest at the left lower sternal border. The infant is currently asymptomatic, feeding well, and has normal oxygen saturations. Which of the following is the most common congenital heart disease (CHD) encountered in the general pediatric population?

A 9-year-old child is brought to the clinic by their parents due to a patch of hair loss on the back of the head that has been expanding over the past two weeks. On physical examination, the physician observes a well-demarcated, ring-shaped area of alopecia. Within the ring, the skin is covered in fine, grey-white scales, and several hairs appear broken off close to the surface, appearing as "black dots." There is mild associated itching. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old male is brought to the Emergency Department with crushing sub-sternal chest pain radiating to his jaw and epigastrium. An ECG reveals ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, consistent with an Acute Inferior Myocardial Infarction. His blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg and his heart rate is 52 bpm. Which of the following medications is a standard part of the Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) protocol for this patient?

A 22-year-old male athlete is evaluated after experiencing a syncopal episode during a basketball game. He reports occasional exertional chest pain. Physical examination reveals a harsh systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur at the left lower sternal border that increases in intensity when the patient stands up from a squatting position. An echocardiogram confirms asymmetrical septal hypertrophy. Which of the following is the first-line pharmacological management for this patient?

A 48-year-old female with a known history of Mitral Stenosis (MS) presents to the emergency department after coughing up several milliliters of bright red blood (hemoptysis). She reports progressive shortness of breath and orthopnea over the past six months. On examination, a loud S1 and a mid-diastolic rumble with an opening snap are heard at the apex. Which of the following is the most likely physiological cause of hemoptysis in this patient?

answers.option: Rupture of the connection between pulmonary and bronchial arterioles

question: A 42-year-old female with a long-standing history of Rheumatic Heart Disease and severe Mitral Stenosis presents for a follow-up. She reports worsening shortness of breath on minimal exertion and recent-onset abdominal bloating and pedal edema. Physical examination reveals a loud S1 and a diastolic rumble at the apex. On neck examination, you observe a prominent V-wave in the Jugular Venous Pressure (JVP) along with a pulsatile liver. Which of the following complications best indicates the progression of her disease to involve pulmonary hypertension and right-sided heart failure?

answers.option: Systemic embolization of the vegetation on the mitral valve
Development of a mid-systolic click and late systolic murmur
RV infarction secondary to Left Coronary Artery (LCA) stenosis
Giant V-wave in JVP due to Tricuspid Regurgitation from pulmonary hypertension

question: A 45-year-old female presents to the emergency department with a 12-hour history of severe, constant epigastric pain that radiates to her back. The pain is associated with repeated bouts of vomiting. On examination, she is tachycardic and has significant tenderness in the upper abdomen. Laboratory studies show a serum amylase level that is only mildly elevated (less than three times the upper limit of normal). Her C-Reactive Protein (CRP) level is measured at 160 mg/L. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to assess the severity and presence of complications?

A 6-month-old infant is brought to the pediatric clinic for a routine check-up. The mother reports that the child seems to tire easily during feedings and has frequent respiratory infections. On cardiovascular examination, the physician notes a loud, continuous "machine-like" murmur heard best at the left infraclavicular area. The infant also has bounding peripheral pulses and a wide pulse pressure. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old male is referred to a cardiologist for evaluation of high blood pressure discovered during a sports physical. He mentions that he frequently experiences "heavy" or aching legs and cold feet after running. On physical examination, the physician notes strong, pounding pulses in the radial and carotid arteries, but the femoral and popliteal pulses are markedly diminished and delayed (radio-femoral delay). Blood pressure in the right arm is 160/95 mmHg, while the blood pressure in the left leg is 105/70 mmHg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old female is brought to the Emergency Department with a high-grade fever (103.5°F), a "sunburn-like" rash covering her trunk and extremities, and a blood pressure of 80/50 mmHg. She reports feeling fine until 24 hours ago when she developed sudden-onset vomiting and diarrhea. On examination, there is significant mucosal hyperemia and evidence of multi-organ involvement (elevated creatinine and liver enzymes). She mentions she is currently on her menstrual cycle and has been using high-absorbency tampons. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old female with a history of severe rheumatic mitral stenosis is scheduled to undergo a percutaneous mitral balloon valvuloplasty. She currently has a low-grade fever, and a recent echocardiogram revealed a small (<5 mm) vegetation on the mitral valve, though she has no history of embolic events. The clinical team is reviewing the current guidelines for infective endocarditis (IE) prevention. According to the Modified Duke Criteria and current AHA/ACC guidelines, which of the following best describes the primary indication for short-term prophylactic antibiotics in a patient with valvular heart disease?

answers.option: Prophylaxis is indicated only for patients with a history of rheumatic fever without current valvular involvement.
Prophylaxis is indicated for high-risk patients (e.g., prosthetic valves, previous IE) undergoing dental procedures involving gingival manipulation.
Prophylaxis is indicated for all patients with mitral stenosis undergoing routine gastrointestinal endoscopy or colonoscopy.
Prophylaxis is indicated for all patients with any form of valvular heart disease undergoing any invasive procedure.
Prophylaxis is indicated only if the vegetation is larger than 10 mm or if there is a history of systemic emboli.

question: A 62-year-old male presents for a routine evaluation of chronic, primary Mitral Regurgitation (MR). He reports a gradual decrease in his exercise tolerance and the recent onset of mild orthopnea. On physical examination, the physician notes a pansystolic murmur at the apex that radiates to the axilla. Which of the following sets of physical examination findings most reliably indicates the progression to severe mitral regurgitation?

answers.option: Non-displaced apex beat and an S4 heart sound
Hyperdynamic apex beat in the 5th intercostal space, midclavicular line
Tapping apex beat with a loud S1
Displaced apex beat and an S3 heart sound
Non-palpable apex beat and a soft S2

question: A 45-year-old male with a history of chronic alcohol use disorder is diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and started on a standard four-drug Anti-Tubercular Therapy (ATT) regimen (Isoniazid, Rifampin, Pyrazinamide, and Ethambutol). Two months into his treatment, he presents with progressive numbness, "pins and needles" sensations (paresthesia), and a burning feeling in his feet and hands. On examination, there is a symmetrical "glove-and-stocking" sensory loss and diminished deep tendon reflexes. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his neurological symptoms?

A 58-year-old male with a 15-year history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus presents to the Emergency Department with a 2-day history of high-grade fever, chills, and severe pain in his right knee. The pain started suddenly and has made it impossible for him to bear weight. He is currently halfway through a course of antibiotics for a culture-confirmed urinary tract infection (UTI). On examination, the right knee is exquisitely tender, erythematous, and significantly swollen with a large effusion. Both active and passive ranges of motion are severely restricted due to pain. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old male presents with chronic fatigue, joint pain (specifically in the second and third metacarpophalangeal joints), and a recent diagnosis of Type 2 Diabetes. On physical examination, the physician notes a subtle grayish-bronze skin pigmentation and mild hepatomegaly. Laboratory studies show mildly elevated ALT and AST. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial screening test for the suspected diagnosis of Hereditary Hemochromatosis?

answers.option: Liver biopsy with Prussian blue staining

question: A 7-year-old girl is brought to the clinic by her parents because she has become increasingly clumsy and has difficulty climbing stairs. During the examination, the physician observes the patient using her hands to "walk up" her own legs to reach a standing position (Gowers' sign). On further inspection, she has a dusky, violaceous rash on her eyelids and scaly, erythematous papules over the dorsal surfaces of her metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints (Gottron papules). Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the diagnosis?

A 52-year-old male with a 20-year history of heavy alcohol consumption presents with chronic, dull epigastric pain that intermittently radiates to his back. He reports a 15-pound weight loss over the past four months and describes his stools as being voluminous, foul-smelling, and difficult to flush. Laboratory studies reveal a fecal elastase level of <100 μg/g (Normal: >200 μg/g) and an HbA1c of 7.8%. An abdominal X-ray shows diffuse punctate calcifications in the upper abdomen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old female with a 10-year history of Ulcerative Colitis presents for a routine follow-up. She reports progressive fatigue and intense pruritus (itching) that is worse at night. On physical examination, she is visibly jaundiced, and multiple excoriations (scratch marks) are noted on her arms and legs. Laboratory studies reveal a significantly elevated Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) and an increased Direct Bilirubin. An MRCP (Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography) shows multiple short, segment strictures and "beading" of both the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old female presents with a several-month history of difficulty swallowing solid foods and persistent heartburn. She also describes her fingers turning white, then blue, and finally red when exposed to cold temperatures (Raynaud’s phenomenon). On physical examination, the physician notes tight, thickened skin over her fingers and toes, as well as multiple small, blanched red spots (telangiectasias) on her face and palms. Laboratory studies are positive for Antinuclear Antibodies (ANA) with a speckled pattern and Anti-centromere antibodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old male, who was a first responder at a nuclear power plant accident ten years ago, presents for a routine physical. He has been closely monitored for long-term health effects related to high-dose ionizing radiation exposure. While he is currently asymptomatic, his physician discusses the risks of radiation-induced secondary malignancies. Historically, which of the following is considered the most common non-solid malignancy to develop following significant acute radiation exposure?

A 65-year-old male presents with a 6-month history of progressive numbness and a "crawling" sensation in his feet. He also reports increasing difficulty with balance, especially when walking in the dark. On examination, he has a wide-based ataxic gait and a positive Romberg sign. Neurological testing reveals a symmetrical loss of vibration and position sense in the lower extremities, along with hyperreflexia and an upgoing plantar response (Babinski sign). Which of the following vitamin deficiencies is most likely responsible for this pattern of demyelination in the distal nerves and spinal cord?

A 45-year-old male presents with a 6-month history of progressive difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids. He notes that he often has to drink large amounts of water to "push the food down" and frequently experiences regurgitation of undigested food at night. A chest X-ray is performed, which reveals a dilated esophagus with an air-fluid level seen behind the heart shadow. On a barium swallow, a "bird’s beak" appearance is noted at the lower esophageal sphincter (LES). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with several small, painless bumps on his torso and inner thighs that have been present for three months. On physical examination, the physician observes multiple 2–5 mm, flesh-colored, dome-shaped papules with a central indentation (umbilication). The child’s mother mentions that his older brother had similar spots after their last swimming lesson. Which of the following is the most correct statement regarding this condition?

answers.option: It is a bacterial infection caused by Staphylococcus aureus
It is a viral infection caused by an RNA virus
It responds effectively to treatment with systemic acyclovir
It presents as flesh-colored, hemispheric-shaped papules with a central dimple
Itching is a prominent and diagnostic feature

question: A 34-year-old female presents with a persistent, symmetrical erythematous rash involving her nose, cheeks, and forehead. She notes that the redness worsens after eating spicy foods or drinking a glass of wine. On physical examination, you observe multiple telangiectasias over the malar area, but notably, there are no comedones. The patient also complains of a "gritty" sensation in her eyes, light sensitivity (photophobia), and you observe redness and crusting along her eyelid margins. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old female presents with a several-month history of joint pain involving her wrists and small joints of the hands, similar to rheumatoid arthritis. She also reports that her fingers turn pale and numb when she reaches into her freezer (Raynaud’s phenomenon). Recently, she has developed difficulty swallowing solid foods and persistent heartburn. Physical examination reveals swelling of the fingers ("puffy fingers") and mild muscle tenderness in her proximal upper arms. Laboratory studies show a positive ANA and remarkably high titers of Anti-U1 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) antibodies, while antibodies to dsDNA, Sm, and Scl-70 are negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old male with a 20-pack-year smoking history presents with a chronic, productive cough that has persisted for the past three years, occurring for at least three consecutive months each year. He reports increasing shortness of breath upon exertion. Physical examination reveals a "stocky" build, mild cyanosis of the lips, and coarse rhonchi on lung auscultation. A biopsy of the central airways is performed. Which of the following histological findings is most characteristic of this patient's primary condition?

answers.option: Hypertrophy and hyperplasia of mucus-secreting glands in the submucosa
Non-caseating granulomas with multinucleated giant cells
Extensive alveolar destruction and interstitial fibrosis
Patchy chronic inflammation with smooth muscle hypertrophy and eosinophils
Abnormal, permanent enlargement of air spaces distal to the terminal bronchioles

question: A 54-year-old male with poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes presents to the Emergency Department with high-grade fever, chills, and a cough productive of copious amounts of foul-smelling sputum. His oxygen saturation is 89% on room air. A chest X-ray reveals a dense mid-zone opacity with a visible air-fluid level, suggestive of a lung abscess. Which of the following groups of organisms is associated with the highest mortality rate in diabetic patients presenting with severe necrotizing pneumonia or lung abscess?

A 68-year-old female presents to her primary care physician for a routine check-up. She has a history of osteoporosis and lives in a northern climate with limited sun exposure. Laboratory studies reveal a low serum calcium level of 8.2 mg/dL (Normal: 8.5–10.5 mg/dL) and an elevated Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) level. Her serum phosphate is also low. Which of the following is the most common underlying cause of chronic calcium deficiency in the general population?

A 45-year-old male with a history of tuberculosis is currently being treated with a multi-drug regimen including Isoniazid. Over the past few weeks, he has developed a "pins and needles" sensation and numbness in a "stocking-and-glove" distribution involving his hands and feet. On examination, there is a symmetrical decrease in sensation to pinprick and vibration. Which of the following vitamin deficiencies is the most likely cause of his peripheral neuropathy?

A 32-year-old male presents with a 3-month history of low-grade fever, night sweats, and unintentional weight loss. He reports progressive, dull abdominal pain, increasing abdominal girth (distension), and alternating bouts of constipation and diarrhea. On examination, the patient appears cachectic and pale. Notably, there is "guttering" in the supraclavicular fossa (significant wasting of the supraclavicular muscles) and a "doughy" feel to the abdomen on palpation. Laboratory studies show a microcytic anemia and a markedly elevated ESR (85 mm/hr). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following conditions present as patches of hair loss with scaling on the affected areas?
Which of the following is the most common initial presenting symptom of bronchial carcinoma?

A 64-year-old man, a known smoker, came to the outpatient department with a complaint of chronic cough. He also had vocal cord paralysis. The workup revealed a 1.8 cm lesion in the middle zone of the left lung. What is the most appropriate treatment?
Considering the effect of genetic and environmental factors on the development of cancer, which of the following has the strongest association with tobacco smoking?
A young boy presents to the outpatient department with itchy patches of hair loss. The areas are well-demarcated, non-inflammatory, and have fine grey scales. What could be the likely diagnosis?

A man comes to the outpatient department with severe itching all over his body. His young nephews also have similar symptoms. On examination, there are scratch marks with burrows in finger webs. What would be the appropriate treatment in this case?

answers.option: Vaseline twice daily for at least a fortnight

question: A middle-aged man presents to OPD with shortness of breath. On examination, there are decreased breath sounds on the right lower lung with a hyperresonant percussion note. What could be the likely diagnosis?

A young female with, a known case of asthma, presents with weakness in her upper limbs. On examination, skin nodules on her lower legs can be appreciated. Workup shows increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and eosinophilia. What could be the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old male comes to the outpatient department, with a history of recurrent chest infections. He also has a history of persistent diarrhea and infertility. His chest X-ray reveals bronchiectasis. Which of the following organisms is associated with poor prognosis in this man?

A young female presents to OPD with complaints of shortness of breath and dry cough for 2 weeks. On examination, she has bilateral crepitations and velcro-like rales in the lower lung fields. She also has pedal edema. what could be the likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most accurate treatment for complicated scabies?
Which of the following anti-tuberculosis drugs can cause thrombocytopenia?

A laborer working in the fields during hot weather presented to the emergency department after he collapsed. His urine output was minimal and he was progressing towards anuria. Which of the following complications is this patient likely to develop?
Which of the following is an incorrect statement regarding the autosomal recessive pattern of inheritance?

answers.option: Males and females are equally affected
The chances of an unaffected child, with an affected sibling, being a carrier is 2/3.
Alleles of a gene must be mutated before the disease manifests in an individual

question: Which of the following sets most accurately defines heat stroke?
Which of the following modalities is used to detect metastasis in bronchogenic carcinoma?

answers.option: Combined Computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography (PET)

question: A female presents to the clinic with right upper quadrant pain and jaundice. On abdominal examination, there is tender hepatomegaly and laboratory results reveal positive anti-smooth muscle antibody (ASMA). What is the likely diagnosis?
A patient presents with bone pain and osteopenia on X-ray. What is the most appropriate step to establish a diagnosis?
Which of the following is an accurate method to monitor response in sarcoidosis?
A low-lying lens can be seen in which of the following metabolic conditions?
Which of the following is the best surgery for obesity with the least adverse effects?
A patient presents with severe nodulocystic acne on the face and trunk. Which of the following is the appropriate treatment in this case?
A patient comes to the clinic suspected of small bowel bacterial overgrowth. Which of the following investigations will help in reaching to the diagnosis?

answers.option: Stool DR and culture and sensitivity (C/S)

question: A patient who is a known case of asthma, presented with symptoms of stable angina. Which of the following will be the preferred treatment in this case?
Which of the following is an appropriate period after which a person is considered non-infectious after starting anti-tuberculosis therapy?

A woman complained of multiple small joint pain, fever, and malar rash. Her urine analysis revealed proteinuria 1+. Which of the following is the best investigation for monitoring disease progression in this patient?
A young lady presented with pain in multiple joints. On examination, her metacarpophalangeal joints were red and swollen. Which of the following investigations would help in confirming the diagnosis?
Extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB) is resistant to which of the following drugs?

A 45-year-old female presents to her physician with the complaint of difficulty climbing stairs for 3 weeks. She complains of mild fever and fatigue as well. A probable diagnosis of dermatomyositis is made. Which of the following investigations can be used to confirm the diagnosis?

A patient who has been a chronic smoker presents to the pulmonology department with a central lung tumor, which is also causing vocal paralysis. What would be the appropriate treatment for this patient?

A patient with a known case of chronic liver disease presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain, distended abdomen, and fever. On examination, there are massive ascites and paracentesis reveals a cloudy peritoneal fluid, containing 1000 WBCs/microlitre with 70% neutrophils. what could be the most likely diagnosis?

A patient came to the outpatient department with routine blood tests and a hepatitis B profile. Hepatitis B profile shows anti-HBs positive, and anti-HBc (IgG) negative. Accordingly, which of the following states corresponds best to this profile?
A 50-year-old man who is diagnosed with chronic liver disease presents to the emergency department with massive hematemesis. Which of the following is the likely cause of this presentation?

A patient complains of bony swellings at the distal interphalangeal (DIP) and proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints. His X-ray reveals a characteristic gull-wing appearance most marked at the second DIP joint. What could be the likely diagnosis?
A 40-year-old alcoholic patient, who is also hypertensive, presents with excessive pain and inflammation of the big toe. What would be the appropriate treatment for this patient?

A 30-year-old female, in her third trimester of pregnancy, presents to the emergency department with complaints of vomiting, right upper quadrant pain, distended abdomen, and jaundice. Which of the following is the likely cause of her presentation?
Which of the following is used to prevent spontaneous bacterial peritonitis?
Which of the following is the management for acute hepatitis B infection?
Which type of shock has warm peripheries as one of its clinical signs?

An electrocardiogram of a patient shows broad complex tachycardia. The man was previously diagnosed with ischemic heart disease. He now presents with dyspnea followed by syncope, with a blood pressure of 60/50. What is the most appropriate treatment in this case

A pregnant woman presents to the outpatient department with complaints of shortness of breath. On precordial examination, a mid-diastolic murmur is heard. Which of the following could be the underlying cause of this murmur?

A patient was admitted to the hospital for an anterior wall myocardial infarction. On 3rd day after treatment, he developed chest pain and shortness of breath. An immediate ECG shows concave ST-elevations in all leads except lead II. Which of the following could be the most likely diagnosis
Which of the following is the most common cause of sudden cardiac death after an acute myocardial infarction?
Which of the following is a common cause of pansystolic murmur after an episode of acute myocardial infarction?
Which of the following is the correct criteria for definitive infective endocarditis?

answers.option: one major and one minor criteria
two minor and four minor criteria

question: A patient comes to the outpatient department complaining of dry mouth and occasional pain in her small joints. She also complains of diarrhea since childhood. What could be the underlying problem in this patient?

answers.option: Sjögren’s syndrome with Systemic lupus erythematosus

question: Regarding the HLA gene, which of the following is accurate?

answers.option: HLA-B27 in ankylosing spondylitis and 5% inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)
HLA DR4 in 50% of rheumatoid arthritis and associated with good prognosis

question: A patient presents to the clinic with features suggestive of mental retardation. On examination, the doctor observes hypopigmentation, calf swelling, and downward dislocation of the lens. Which of the following conditions explains his features?
Which drug improves mortality and reduces remodeling after myocardial infarction?

A young male presented with complaints of on-and-off fever for 1 week. He also has RUQ pain. On examination, he has tenderness to palpitation in RUQ. X-ray shows elevated right hemi diaphragm. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man came to the outpatient department with the complaint of on and off loose stools for 1 year. He is unwell. On examination, he is severely cachectic and anemic. Laboratory investigations reveal hemoglobin: 8.2g/dL, WBC: 2000/mm3, platelets: 98000 per microlitre. Colonoscopy shows ileocecal stricture. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A patient was diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and started on quadruple therapy. When, after starting treatment, can the patient be said to be non-infectious?
What should be the most appropriate treatment for a known patient of hepatitis B for four years? Serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase is 1600 units per liter of serum.

A 60-year-old man presents to the emergency with a blood pressure of 80/60 and chest pain with dizziness. His ECG shows wide and bizarre QRS complexes. What is the best treatment option for this patient?
A man who is a known case of ischemic heart disease came to the clinic with complaints of dyspepsia. Which of the following is least likely to be associated with dyspepsia?

A young female with a known case of asthma, controlled by salbuterol and salmeterol/fluticasone, presents with complaints of increased episodes during daytime and frequent nighttime awakening due to symptoms. What should be the next best step in management?
Which of the following is true regarding X-linked dominant inheritance?

answers.option: An affected father will have 50% daughters affected
An affected father will have all affected daughters
Males are affected more severely than females
An affected mother will always have an affected son.
An affected mother will never have an affected son.

question: A 32-year-old male presents to the clinic with symptoms of cough, weight loss, and fever for the past two months. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds and scattered crackles in the left lung. A chest x-ray shows consolidation in the left lung. A sputum culture test is positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis. What is the appropriate treatment?

answers.option: RIPE for 2 months, followed by rifampin + isoniazid for 4 months
Isoniazid + rifampin for 4 months followed RIPE for 2 months

question: A 35-year-old male patient with a fever and pleuritic chest pain present to the emergency department. His ECG shows diffuse ST elevations and PR depression. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A newborn baby is noted to have a flat facial profile, a single crease across the palm of the hand, and a gap between the first and second toes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man comes to the clinic with a fever, cough productive of green sputum, and difficulty breathing. His oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. He has no underlying lung conditions and has not traveled recently. A chest x-ray shows an area of consolidation in the right lower lobe. What is the best treatment choice for this patient?

A 65-year-old man with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma receives CHOP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone) regimen as part of his chemotherapy treatment. Two weeks after completing the regimen, he develops hematuria and severe abdominal pain. What could have prevented this complication?

A 17-year-old boy presents with low-grade fever, cough, and difficulty breathing for the past week. He has associated fatigue and appears jaundiced. Liver function tests show an AST of 110 and an ALT of 95. A chest x-ray shows interstitial infiltrates. He has not traveled recently and has not been exposed to any known infectious sources. Which organism is most likely responsible?
